purpose: Prevents an API from being tricked into making unauthorized requests to internal systems or arbitrary external destinations on the attacker's behalf.
summary: Server Side Request Forgery occurs when an API fetches a remote resource (a URL, webhook, or file) without validating the user-supplied destination, allowing an attacker to redirect the server into calling internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other unintended targets.
expectedStatementElements: Which API features accept a user-supplied URL or destination (webhooks, file imports, link previews, PDF generation, etc.)
How those destinations are validated or restricted before the server makes the request (allow-lists, blocking internal IP ranges, disabling redirects)
Whether internal network segmentation limits what an SSRF exploit could actually reach even if a request is forced through
How the API is tested for SSRF (e.g., pointing a webhook or URL field at an internal address or cloud metadata service)
evidenceExamples: Inventory of endpoints/features that fetch remote resources based on user input
URL validation or allow-list configuration for outbound requests initiated by the API
Network segmentation documentation showing what internal resources are reachable from the API server
Security test results attempting SSRF against a webhook, import, or preview feature
commonGaps: Webhook or URL-fetching features accept any destination with no validation or allow-listing
No blocking of requests to internal IP ranges, localhost, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254)
Redirects aren't restricted, so a validated URL can redirect the server somewhere unintended
No testing has attempted to point a user-controlled URL field at an internal resource
interviewQuestions: Which features let a user supply a URL that your server then fetches on their behalf?
What stops that feature from being pointed at an internal service or the cloud metadata endpoint?
If a validated URL responded with a redirect, would your server follow it somewhere unintended?
Has anyone actually tested these features for SSRF by targeting an internal address?
